findings.highlight: to stop the cause of this
findings.evidenceJa: この凶行を止める為に
findings.governingReading: Shirou calls Saber in order to stop this atrocity or outrage.
findings.explanation: Cause of this replaces the wrongdoing itself with an unspecified cause, weakening why Shirou chooses to command Saber.

findings.governingReading: A distortion or undulation appears in space as the Command Spell vanishes.
findings.explanation: A winding is malformed and does not clearly convey space itself warping.

findings.evidenceJa: 文字通り、それは魔法だったのだろう
findings.governingReading: Shirou supposes that, literally, it was probably magic.
findings.explanation: Sorcery substitutes a loaded technical English term and removes the sentence’s literal framing in a passage adjacent to Fate’s Magecraft and Magic distinction.

findings.highlight: My organs will explode from the impact.
findings.evidenceJa: 落下の衝撃でのきなみ内臓がイカレてしまう
findings.governingReading: The impact of the fall wrecks Shirou’s internal organs across the board.
findings.explanation: Explode invents a specific catastrophic mechanism and shifts the ongoing result into the future.

findings.evidenceJa: セイバーは仕方なげに言葉を飲んでくれた
findings.governingReading: Apparently grasping Shirou’s resolve, Saber reluctantly swallows what she was going to say.
findings.explanation: Generic acceptance removes her reluctance and continued objection to leaving his lethal wounds untreated.

findings.governingReading: Shirou assigns Saber to defeat Rider while he will strike or take down Shinji.
findings.explanation: Get leaves Shirou’s intended action vague at the moment he accepts his part of the fight.
